statement: Do-not-disturbs opt out more than everyone else when contacted, so churn risk is a signal independent of predicted uplift.
note: The supporting signal for N2. Published at 1.29x after the original 1.93x was found to be a single small-sample draw.

statement: The uplift model's top decile realises more uplift than its bottom decile, in every draw.
Decile uplift is monotone: Spearman >= 0.9 in every draw.
note: Fails at 0.879 on one draw. Reported as failed rather than rounded up; near-monotone is tracked as the weaker claim.

statement: The model-judgement bucket contains a non-trivial count of refusals of customers who would have paid, as the calibration result requires.
The counterfactual's cost-side disagreement with the model-based estimate is a replicated finding.
observed: UNRESOLVED: the realised cost fell outside the model-based cost interval in 3 of 6 draws (including the headline). The cost-side disagreement is NOT established as a replicated finding -- it is a property of which draw is examined, not of the method -- and must be reported as unresolved rather than as either a confirmed finding or a resolved non-finding.
note: Outside the interval in 3 of 6 draws. Unresolved, and published as unresolved — the limitation itself did not replicate.

statement: DR's low reading on Criteo is caused by cross-fitting starving the 15% minority arm, so more folds should shrink the gap.
note: Refuted: coverage and mean gap are flat across a 10x fold range.

statement: Detection latency is claimable: the detector fires in every draw at the largest effect size, reported with its false-alarm rate.
Contact produces incremental revenue, measured on a real randomised experiment with real dollars rather than in the simulator.
note: The only money figure in this repo not produced by its own generator: $424 per 1,000 customers, interval excluding zero.

statement: Targeting beats matched-volume random targeting on real money, not only in simulation.
note: Not established. Three estimators agree on the sign - all the registered rule asked for - but the paired interval on the difference covers zero. The rule was weaker than the question and is left as registered, with the interval reported beside it.

statement: Targeting beats contacting the same number of people at random, on real randomised data rather than in simulation.
note: Held on Criteo under a rule deliberately stricter than Tier 1b's: the paired interval must exclude zero, not merely have three estimators agree on a sign. 8.94 SEs from zero.

statement: Correcting tau_hat's measured over-spread increases incremental recovery.
observed: UNDETERMINED: the draws disagree on the sign, so no effect on recovered value is established. The correction is not shipped on this evidence.
note: Undetermined: the draws disagree on sign. The correction demonstrably works as arithmetic - the held-out slope moves 0.6674 to 0.9508 - and recovered value still does not follow consistently. Improving a diagnostic is not improving the decision.
The project's worst near-miss. Published as dominance from a run that no longer reproduced; it trades, it does not dominate.
